question: When should I give the pre-monsoon Bordeaux mixture spray against coffee leaf rust, and at what strength?
question_en: When should I give the pre-monsoon Bordeaux mixture spray against coffee leaf rust, and at what strength?
gold_answer: Spray 0.5% Bordeaux mixture during April-May, when rust spreads to young leaves; finish the protection by the first week of June.
evidence: Therefore during this period, spray of 0.5% Bordeaux mixture is very important which prevents the spread of disease and protects the young leaves.

question: Should Bordeaux mixture be sprayed on the upper or the lower side of coffee leaves to control rust?
question_en: Should Bordeaux mixture be sprayed on the upper or the lower side of coffee leaves to control rust?
gold_answer: On the lower surface of the leaves; spraying only the upper surface does not protect against the spread of rust.
evidence: Spraying the Bordeaux on the upper surface of the leaves does not ensure protection from the spread of the disease.

question: How many barrels of Bordeaux spray are needed to cover one hectare of coffee?
question_en: How many barrels of Bordeaux spray are needed to cover one hectare of coffee?
gold_answer: About 15 barrels of the spray mixture cover one hectare.
evidence: About 15 barrels of the spray mixture adequately covers one hectare of the area.

question: Can I mix urea into the Bordeaux mixture when spraying for leaf rust?
question_en: Can I mix urea into the Bordeaux mixture when spraying for leaf rust?
gold_answer: No. Adding urea is a bad practice: nitrogen is lost as ammonia and the spray becomes less effective. Only potash (350 g MOP per barrel) is compatible.
evidence: There is a common practice of adding urea to the Bordeaux mixture.
This is a bad practice which should be avoided.

question: What pH should the Bordeaux mixture have?
question_en: What pH should the Bordeaux mixture have?
gold_answer: Between 9 and 10 for the best efficiency.
evidence: Please ensure that the pH of the Bordeaux mixture is maintained between 9 and 10 for the best efficiency of the sprayed mixture.

question: The blossom shower came late and there are no new shoots. What should I spray against leaf rust instead of Bordeaux mixture?
question_en: The blossom shower came late and there are no new shoots. What should I spray against leaf rust instead of Bordeaux mixture?
gold_answer: Avoid Bordeaux; spray a systemic fungicide (160 g Bayleton 25 WP or 400 ml Contaf 5EC in 200 litres of water, 7-8 barrels per hectare) during the break in the monsoon.
evidence: In such an event, spray of 7-8 barrels per hectare systemic fungicides (160 gm of 25 WP 0.02% Bayleton or 400 ml of Contaf-5EC-0.01% in 200 litres of water) during the break in the monsoon which will help in controlling the CLR disease.

question: Which weather conditions favour the early appearance of coffee leaf rust?
question_en: Which weather conditions favour the early appearance of coffee leaf rust?
gold_answer: Humid cool windy weather from May to November with intermittent showers and sunshine, cloudy misty weather with drizzle in February-March, and thin or no overhead shade during the south-west monsoon.
evidence: Thin or no overhead shade during the south-west monsoon is also one of the favourable factors for the development of this disease.

question: When does leaf rust intensify after the monsoon and what should I spray then?
question_en: When does leaf rust intensify after the monsoon and what should I spray then?
gold_answer: Rust intensifies in September; spray 0.5% Bordeaux mixture at 15 barrels per hectare.
evidence: The coffee leaf rust disease intensifies during September month.

question_en: My estate is above 3500 feet. Do I need to worry about leaf rust in February-March?
gold_answer: Generally no: areas above 3500 feet are usually not affected by leaf rust during February-March.
evidence: The areas which are located in elevations more than 3500 feet are generally not affected by leaf rust disease during these months.

question: How do I prepare 0.5% Bordeaux mixture?
question_en: How do I prepare 0.5% Bordeaux mixture?
gold_answer: Dissolve 1 kg copper sulphate in 10 litres of water overnight, dissolve 1 kg spray lime in 10 litres of water, add the lime solution to 180 litres of water and then add the copper sulphate solution while stirring.
evidence: Dissolve 1 kg of pure chemically tested copper sulphate in 10 litres of water by suspending it in a gunny bag or cloth bag overnight.
Similarly prepare spray lime solution by dissolving 1 kg of spray lime in 10 litres of water.

question: For an organic coffee farm, what should be the main way to manage leaf rust?
question_en: For an organic coffee farm, what should be the main way to manage leaf rust?
gold_answer: Planting rust-resistant cultivars should be the main control measure, supported by cultural management, biological control and copper fungicides.
evidence: The use of rust-resistant cultivars as the main control measure for rust management should be prioritized, with incentive programs to replace crops with susceptible cultivars in the various organic coffee-producing countries.

gold_answer: Its larvae feed inside the leaf mesophyll, causing necrosis, loss of photosynthetic capacity, defoliation and yield loss.
evidence: During the immature life stages, the insect feeds in the mesophyll triggering necrosis and causing loss of photosynthetic capacity, defoliation and signiﬁcant yield loss to coffee crops.

question: How should I collect a soil sample from my coffee block?

evidence: Select at random 20 spots in each block, remove surface litter and dig a hole of 9 inches diameter using a suitable tool up to 9 inches depth.

question_en: What spacing should I use when planting Arabica coffee?
gold_answer: Arabica talls 7x7, 7x6 or 6x6 feet; Arabica dwarf or semi-dwarf 5x5 feet.

question: What size of pit should I dig for planting coffee and what should I put in it?
question_en: What size of pit should I dig for planting coffee and what should I put in it?
gold_answer: 1.5 x 1.5 x 1.5 feet pits, weathered for 15-20 days, filled with 1-1.5 kg compost or farmyard manure and 50-100 g rock phosphate mixed with top soil.
evidence: The pits measuring 1.5 X 1.5 X 1.5 feet length, breadth and depth are ideal for planting.

question: How should I water young coffee plants after the monsoon ends?
question_en: How should I water young coffee plants after the monsoon ends?
gold_answer: Give 5-10 litres of water per plant once a week.
evidence: After the cessation of monsoon, it is recommended that young coffee plants should be irrigated with 5 to 10 litres water per plant once in a week.

question: How much nitrogen should I apply during the break in the monsoon?
question_en: How much nitrogen should I apply during the break in the monsoon?
gold_answer: 58 kg nitrogen per hectare (2.5 bags of urea), which also reduces berry drop.
evidence: Therefore, apply 58 kgs of nitrogen (2.5 bags of Urea) per hectare during the break in the monsoon.

question: Which slope directions (aspects) are suitable for a new coffee plantation?
question_en: Which slope directions (aspects) are suitable for a new coffee plantation?
gold_answer: North, east and north-east aspects; western aspects need thick shade because of the scorching sun.
evidence: North, East and North-East aspects are suitable for growing coffee.

question: What soil mixture should I fill in coffee nursery bags?
question_en: What soil mixture should I fill in coffee nursery bags?
gold_answer: 6 parts sieved jungle soil, 2 parts well-rotted cattle manure or compost and 1 part coarse river sand (never sea sand).
evidence: A nursery mixture of 6 parts of sieved jungle soil( free from nematodes and other pests), two parts of well rotted cattle manure or compost and one part of coarse river sand (do not use sea sand as it contains sodium which is harmful to the seedlings) should be prepared and mixed well to fill the nursery bags.

question: How many leaves should I send for leaf nutrient analysis?
question_en: How many leaves should I send for leaf nutrient analysis?
gold_answer: At least 25 pairs of leaves (the fourth pair from the tip) per hectare, collected before 10 a.m.
evidence: A minimum of 25 pairs of leaves from one hectare land is necessary for precise analysis.

question: To what moisture level should parchment coffee be dried?
question_en: To what moisture level should parchment coffee be dried?
gold_answer: To 11.0% moisture.
evidence: The superficial water content should be removed by spreading the parchment over wire mesh trays and then dried on clean cement or clay lined drying yards till the moisture content reaches a value of 11.0%.

question: When are Robusta flower buds ready for blossom irrigation?
question_en: When are Robusta flower buds ready for blossom irrigation?
gold_answer: Generally between 15 February and 15 March.
evidence: Generally between February 15th and March 15th flower buds will mature and will be ready for blooming in Robusta coffee.
